title: Learning / Theory
description: Understand the core concepts of Binary Heaps (Min Heap and Max Heap), their implementations, and properties.
identify: Problems asking to build a heap from an array
Implementing heap operations like insert, extract min/max, or heapify
appearsIn: System design primitives for priority queues
explanation: A Heap is a special Tree-based data structure in which the tree is a complete binary tree. Max-Heap guarantees the parent is greater than its children, while Min-Heap guarantees the parent is smaller.

title: Medium Problems
description: Application of Priority Queues to solve problems involving top K elements, merging arrays, and scheduling.
identify: Sort elements based on frequency or rank
explanation: Medium problems typically utilize the standard library priority queue (`std::priority_queue` in C++) to keep track of the largest or smallest elements seen so far optimally in O(log K) time per insertion.

title: Hard Problems
description: Complex algorithms involving dual heaps, custom comparators, or integrating heaps with other data structures like maps.
identify: Finding the running median of a data stream
Tracking top K elements dynamically with combinations or streams
explanation: Hard heap problems often require maintaining two heaps to balance data (like the Median Finder problem) or mapping objects to priority levels dynamically using structs and custom comparators.
